sanskrit_verse:
क्रमाद् अभ्यागतं द्रव्यं हृतम् अपि उद्धरेत् तु यः ।
दायादेभ्यो न तद् दद्याद् विद्यया लब्धम् एव च ॥
transliteration: kramād abhyāgataṃ dravyaṃ hṛtam api uddharet tu yaḥ | dāyādebhyaḥ na tat dadyād vidyayā labdham eva ca ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who retrieves property obtained through sequential rightful means, even if previously taken, shall restore it—not to heirs or successors—but exclusively through the capacity by which it was originally acquired via knowledge.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority derived from the method of acquisition
Causation rooted in sequential dharmic action
Restoration logic prioritizing original mode of attainment
Consciousness alignment through retracing causal sequence
executable_legal_axioms: IF an asset is recovered AND its prior possession involved sequential dharmic process THEN return shall be executed solely to the knower-acquirer.
IF claimant lacks vidyā-equivalent capacity THEN disallow inheritance-based restitution.
IF retrieval occurs post-loss THEN restoration pathway must mirror original acquisition mechanism.
IF dispute arises THEN adjudicate based on pramāṇa of vidyā, not lineage or succession.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that restitution rights are not inheritable but are bound to the consciousness-capacity of the original acquirer. Legal thresholds must prioritize epistemic authority over genealogical claims when determining legitimate ownership restoration.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality confirms that rightful ownership flows from vidyā, not bloodline. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures sequential manifestation aligns with dāna-dharma. Responsibility is proportional to the clarity of knowing; hence, no punitive consequence attaches—only realignment of possession with knowing-consciousness.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate retrieval protocol aligned with original vidyā-based acquisition method
Verify claimant's vidyā equivalence before executing transfer
Reconstruct causal chain using pramāṇa-based inquiry
Execute reintegration without punitive overlays, restoring energetic integrity
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority: Property belongs to the consciousness that knows it. Dharma is restored through vidyā-bound pathways. There is no punishment—only alignment of possession with knowing. Consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
